gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is rated to operate only up to 40 °C (104 °F), or that at its 20 A solar-input limit the panel array must run at 50 V or more to reach the advertised 1,000 W.
standout_why: Compared against dealectric.com (ours, 2026-11-04), backup-power.org/best-solar-generator-kits and energysage.com/energy-storage/solar-generators-overview. None of them gives an operating or charging temperature ceiling for any candidate. Our page only quotes Jackery storage temperatures, and EnergySage only says fans run. backup-power.org does print the Elite 200 V2 input limits (12 to 60 V, 20 A) and explains series wiring, but only for the AC180's 10 A limit. It never says what 20 A means for adding panels to the Elite 200 V2, so the wiring point is only partly new. The Good Housekeeping page could not be fetched.
decides: Confirms the Elite 200 V2 as the pick and adds two rules for using it. First, it should run and charge somewhere below 104 °F, which means in the shade and not in a closed garage, car or sunny spot next to the panels during a hot post-storm cleanup. Second, the 400–800 W of panels ChatGPT suggests only helps if the array keeps its open-circuit voltage at or below 60 V and its current at or below 20 A. Low-voltage folding panels wired in parallel hit the 20 A limit long before 1,000 W, so extra panels mostly need to go in series. The 2×200 W kit page lists no series or parallel connector in the box.

findings.note: Quoted from the page FAQ: 'Elite 200 V2: 12V-60V/20A, 1,000W max'. Arithmetic: 1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V, so the array must run at 50 V or more under load to reach 1,000 W, while its open-circuit voltage stays at or below 60 V. Panels in parallel add current, panels in series add voltage.
